parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The binding's name on these routes: the host's device id for the printer it shows while that printer has one binding, and <device id>@<light>:<segment> once it has two. GET /bindings carries every binding's id.

get.summary: The layout one binding composes with, and where each value came from
get.description: A layout is per binding, because a 256x64 panel and a 48-LED strip do not compose the same way and two bindings on one light can be laid out differently. Every value in the answer carries the origin it came from: store when this binding has a row in this module's configuration store, default when it has none. A binding nobody has laid out therefore answers the built-in default rather than null or an empty object, which is what lets a screen offer a reset on exactly the values that have something to reset. Nothing here reads the light. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The layout in force for this binding.

light.description: The light the binding sits on, named the way GET /controllers names one.

persisted.description: True when this module has a store to keep a change in.

note.description: What this build does with the layout, and why a change here could not be kept when it could not.

404.description: This module drives no binding of that name (BINDING_NOT_FOUND).

503.description: This module's configuration store cannot be read (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

put.summary: Set the layout one binding composes with
put.description: Writes one binding's layout and replaces the row it had, so a field the body leaves out goes back to the built-in default: a bar at the bottom twelve rows thick, the percentage at the largest scale this build draws, the job name, and take-turns every fifteen seconds. bar_band is top or bottom; bar_rows is 1 to 48 of a 64-row panel; percent_scale is 3, 4 or 5; rotation is take-turns or side-by-side; rotate_seconds is one or more; remaining may only be false, because this build draws no time remaining and a key that asks for a picture it will not draw is refused rather than ignored. side-by-side is drawn: the digits sit on the left and the job's name on the right, cut to the room the digits leave, and the answer says so. Whether a layout fits the panel it is pointed at is judged where the panel's own height is known, at the frame, and refused there rather than cropped. Nothing is sent to the light. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The layout was written and is the one this binding has.

applied.description: True when the layout is the one written.

persisted.description: Always true here: the row was written into this module's own store.

note.description: What was written, and what it does not yet change.

400.description: The body is not a layout: not JSON, a key this module does not read, or none of the eight keys (LAYOUT_BODY_INVALID). Nothing was changed.

404.description: This module drives no binding of that name (BINDING_NOT_FOUND).

409.description: A band this build does not know, a bar taller than the panel can spare, a scale outside 3-5, a rotation that is neither take-turns nor side-by-side, a rotation of no seconds, or remaining asked for on a build that draws none (LAYOUT_REFUSED). Nothing was changed.

503.description: This module has no store to write to (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

delete.summary: Put one binding back to the built-in layout
delete.description: Removes the stored row for one binding, so it composes with the default again. A binding with no row is not an error: the answer says removed: false beside the default it was already using, because a screen distinguishing "already at the default" from "no such binding" needs those to be different answers. Nothing is sent to the light. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The row is gone and the binding is at its default.

removed.description: True when there was a stored row and it was taken away.

404.description: This module drives no binding of that name (BINDING_NOT_FOUND).

503.description: This module has no store to write to (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The binding's name on these routes: the host's device id for the printer it shows while that printer has one binding, and <device id>@<light>:<segment> once it has two. GET /bindings carries every binding's id.

put.summary: Pause one binding, and leave the rest of the module alone
put.description: Writes one binding's own pause with the absolute instant it ends at. The six lengths are 10m, 1h, 6h, 1d, 3d and forever, and a length outside them is refused by name rather than rounded. A pause switches the light off; a binding that drives one segment of a strip somebody else also drives is handed back instead, because the rest of that strip belongs to its owner — the answer's effect says which of the two this binding is. The light is switched off until that instant passes and then comes back on by itself, with one write and none in between. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The pause was written, with the instant it ends at.

paused.description: True when the pause is in force now.

effect.description: off for a binding that drives its whole light; hands-back for one that drives a borrowed zone.

400.description: The body is not a pause: not JSON, a key this module does not read, or no length at all (PAUSE_BODY_INVALID). Nothing was changed.

404.description: This module drives no binding of that name (BINDING_NOT_FOUND).

409.description: A length that is not one of the six the panic button offers (PAUSE_REFUSED). Nothing was changed.

503.description: This module has no store to write to (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

delete.summary: Take one binding's own pause out of the store
delete.description: Removes one binding's own pause, so nothing will pause that binding on the next start either. A binding with no pause is not an error: the answer says resumed: false. The light is switched back on and its picture is painted again at once. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The pause is gone, or there was none.

resumed.description: True when there was a pause and it was taken away.

404.description: This module drives no binding of that name (BINDING_NOT_FOUND).

503.description: This module has no store to write to (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

parameters.name: light
parameters.description: The light's name: the controller's address without its scheme, as GET /controllers names one.

get.summary: Every binding on one light, each with its layout
get.description: The Layout screen is scoped to one light, so this is the answer it is drawn from: one entry per binding that light carries, in the operator's order, each with every value in force and the origin of each. A stored row naming a binding the running set does not drive is reported in unknown_layouts rather than applied or deleted: a binding that was removed keeps its layout in the file, and adding it back should find it again. Nothing here reads the light. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The light's bindings and their layouts.

unknown_layouts.description: Bindings the store holds a layout for that this module does not drive.

404.description: This module drives no light of that name (CONTROLLER_NOT_FOUND).

503.description: This module's configuration store cannot be read (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

get.summary: The brightness windows, judged at this instant in the timezone setting's zone
get.description: The list the Brightness screen edits, in the operator's order, with the window in force at the instant of the answer named beside it. A window is judged in the IANA zone the timezone setting names and never in this process's own clock, which inside the Prusa Connect container is almost always UTC: a window judged there fires hours away from the evening it was written for, and the answer therefore always carries judged_in and now so that a person can check. A window whose end precedes its start wraps midnight and is accepted; the one whose two ends are the same is refused, because that is either a whole day or no time at all. Overlapping windows are allowed and the first one wins. This build still runs the brightness on the light from the brightness_schedule setting, so this is the list that decides the light's brightness, judged in the module's own timezone setting. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The windows, judged.

409.description: A window in the store is one this module cannot act on (WINDOW_REFUSED).

503.description: This module's configuration store cannot be read (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

post.summary: Add one brightness window to the end of the list
post.description: Adds one window after every other, because the order decides which of two overlapping windows wins and a window added at the front would silently take over moments another one covers. A window is a time range and a brightness: from and to written HH:MM, brightness 0-255, and days optionally. The window cannot be written at all unless the timezone setting names a zone it can be judged in, and the refusal is that setting's own sentence. Nothing is sent to the light. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The window was added, and the whole list is answered.

added.description: The position the new window holds, counting from zero.

400.description: The body is not a brightness window (WINDOW_BODY_INVALID). Nothing was changed.

409.description: Two ends the same, a time of day that is not HH:MM, a brightness outside 0-255, a day that is not one of the seven, or no timezone to judge the window in (WINDOW_REFUSED). Nothing was changed.

503.description: This module has no store to write to (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The window's position in the list, counting from zero, as GET /windows reports it.

put.summary: Replace one brightness window, in place
put.description: Replaces one window whole, at the position it holds, so its place in the order is kept and it takes over nothing it did not already cover. The same rules apply as when a window is added, and nothing is sent to the light. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The window was replaced, and the whole list is answered.

400.description: The body is not a brightness window (WINDOW_BODY_INVALID). Nothing was changed.

404.description: The list holds no window at that position (WINDOW_NOT_FOUND). Nothing was changed.

409.description: The window is not one this module can act on, or there is no timezone to judge it in (WINDOW_REFUSED). Nothing was changed.

503.description: This module has no store to write to (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

delete.description: Removes one window, and every window after it moves up one position: the index is a place in a list and not a minted identity, which the list reports and the answer's note says. Nothing is sent to the light. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The window was removed, and the whole list is answered.

removed.description: True when a window at that position was removed.

404.description: The list holds no window at that position (WINDOW_NOT_FOUND). Nothing was changed.

503.description: This module has no store to write to (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

get.summary: Every pause there is: whether it is on, why, and when it ends
get.description: Answers the three questions the pause has to answer about every one of them — is it on, why, and when exactly it ends, and for forever that it does not — and beside them every binding's own fate, which is where the borrowed-zone exception is visible. A pause is on when the clock is before the instant it ends at: nothing runs a timer, the row carries an absolute instant, and an expired row is still reported with expired: true rather than deleted, because a read is not a write. A binding that drives one segment of a strip somebody else also drives reads effect hands-back and never off. This build does not yet switch a light off. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The pause state, and every binding's fate.

now.description: The instant the answer was made, RFC 3339 in UTC.

paused.description: True when any pause is in force.

why.description: Which scope pauses this module: the global pause or one binding's own.

until.description: When the global pause ends, absent for forever.

paused_by.description: The printers whose own pause is in force, when no global pause is.

borrowed.description: True when this binding drives one zone of a light this module does not own outright.

503.description: This module's configuration store cannot be read (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

put.summary: Pause every binding, for one of the six lengths
put.description: The header's panic button. A pause switches the light off when it is obeyed, one write and then nothing until it ends; a binding that drives a borrowed zone is handed back instead, because powering that controller down would take somebody else's strip with it. The expiry is stored as an absolute instant and not as a length or a timer, so a pause survives a restart and a settings save — this process is rebuilt on both. The light is switched off until that instant passes and then comes back on by itself, with one write and none in between. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The pause was written, with the instant it ends at.

400.description: The body is not a pause: not JSON, a key this module does not read, or no length at all (PAUSE_BODY_INVALID). Nothing was changed.

409.description: A length that is not one of the six (PAUSE_REFUSED). Nothing was changed.

503.description: This module has no store to write to (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

delete.summary: Take the global pause out of the store
delete.description: Removes the global pause, so nothing will pause this module on the next start either. A module with no global pause is not an error: the answer says resumed: false. The light is switched back on and its picture is painted again at once. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The global pause is gone, or there was none.

503.description: This module has no store to write to (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

get.description: The frame this module has decided for the light, the printer it decided it from, how old that reading is, and what the last write to the controller did — so a person can tell what the module thinks without looking at a light. An instance driving one binding answers the frame beside the printer it came from; an instance driving several answers a bindings list, one entry per binding, because one body cannot say which of two lights its frame describes. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The module's answer.

bindings.description: One entry per binding, in the order they first published a frame. Present instead of the single frame below when this module drives more than one binding.

id.description: The host's id for the printer.

name.description: The name an operator gave it.

connected.description: Whether the host holds a session for it now.

retired.description: Whether the id no longer names a machine.

state.description: The last state the printer reported, such as PRINTING.

state_known.description: Whether this build had a reading of that word. False means the printer said something unrecognised, not that it said nothing.

reading.description: How old the newest fact about the printer is.

last_change.description: When anything about the printer last moved, in UTC, and empty when nothing has been reported yet.

observed_at.description: When the reading behind the frame was taken, in UTC.

age_seconds.description: How old last_change was at observed_at, to the millisecond.

stale.description: Whether the newest fact is older than the module's staleness threshold, so no reading describes the printer now.

frame.description: What the light is being asked to show.

colour.description: The colour of the whole range, one byte per channel.

lit.description: How many LEDs, counted from the first, carry the completed part of the job. Zero means the whole range is the colour.

total.description: How many LEDs the range holds, and zero until the controller has said.

percent.description: The completed part of the job in whole percent, or -1 when there is no percentage this module may present: no job on the bed, no live reading, or a progress the guarded reading refused. Not the same as zero, which a paused print at 0 % reports honestly.

name.description: The name the printer gives the job on the bed, such as MK4IS_0.4n_0.2mm_PLA_MK4IS_1h52m.gcode, and empty when there is none or the reading is not live. It is the printer's own string: what a panel draws from it is the layout's business.

reason.description: The rule that decided this frame, such as progress or disconnected. For a log line and for a test, never for a person looking at the light.

last_send.description: What the last write to the controller did, and null before the first one has been attempted.

at.description: When the attempt was made, in UTC.

ok.description: Whether the controller took the frame.

error.description: What went wrong, absent when nothing did.

503.description: The module has not decided a frame yet, which is true only in the moment between its first reading and its first tick (NO_READING_YET).

schema.description: The module's own refusal, as faults.go registers it.

code.description: The registered code, ending in NO_READING_YET.

title.description: The English title of the code.

retryable.description: Whether sending the same request again can work.

get.summary: One picture per binding, for the Overview screen's thumbnails
get.description: One frame per binding this module is drawing, each carrying the frame it decided (colour, fill, total, percent, name and reason), how old the reading behind it is, when it last wrote, and the picture itself as a PNG in base64 - drawn by the same code that draws the light, from the frame the painter decided and not from a second reading of it. A thumbnail is a reconstruction and not a screenshot: this firmware cannot read its pixels back. Nothing on this route opens a socket to a controller, so a light that has stopped answering still has a picture, taken from its last reading, with reading.stale true and its age in reading.age_seconds. A panel is composed exactly as the painter composes it when the layout draws something and the frame is about a job in progress, and is otherwise the panel's own fill; a strip binding that borrows a segment draws only that segment's run. The pictures are cached against the frame that produced them, and image.cached says whether this answer was served from that cache. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: One frame per binding, in the order the bindings first published.

count.description: How many frames are in the list.

note.description: What a thumbnail is, in the words the page repeats: a reconstruction from the frame this module decided, not a screenshot.

503.description: No frame has been decided yet, or the one binding's picture cannot be drawn (NO_READING_YET).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The light's name on these routes: its address without the scheme, so that it is one path segment. http://10.0.0.136 is 10.0.0.136 here, and GET /controllers carries it as name.

get.summary: The snapshots this module holds of one light, newest first
get.description: Every snapshot this module holds for one light, newest first: the id, when it was taken, the light it came from, the file's size, how many presets it holds, and what it does not contain. A snapshot is the light's own /json/cfg, its /presets.json and its /json/state, kept as a file in the directory the module was granted, 0600, one file per snapshot. They live beside this module's configuration document and not in it, and they survive a module purge that the document does not. Nothing on this route opens a socket to a controller: the list exists because a dead light cannot be read, so it has to answer while the light is dead. A file that cannot be decoded is reported in unreadable rather than left out, because a backup somebody believes he has and cannot restore is a fact he needs to see. The omissions are the honest part: no configuration dump on the lights this build was measured against carries the wifi password, so a literal hundred-per-cent clone is impossible over the API. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The snapshots this module holds for this light, and the light's own name and address.

device.description: The light's name on these routes.

address.description: The controller's base URL as an operator wrote it.

persisted.description: False when this module was granted no data directory, in which case no snapshot can be taken or kept.

unreadable.description: Files in the snapshot folder that cannot be decoded, with the reason. Absent when every file reads.

404.description: This module drives no light of that name (CONTROLLER_NOT_FOUND).

503.description: This module's snapshot folder cannot be read (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

post.description: Reads the light and keeps a snapshot of it now: its /json/cfg, its /presets.json, its /json/state and the identity that makes a restore safe - the address this module names it by, the name it calls itself, its firmware, and its shape and pixel count. This is the screen's refresh now, on demand, and it is what an operator takes before changing something on the light or before replacing it. A light that does not answer is refused rather than stored half-read (SNAPSHOT_UNREADABLE); the snapshots already held stay readable, which is the whole reason they are kept. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The snapshot was written and is answered with the id it was given.

404.description: This module drives no light of that name (CONTROLLER_NOT_FOUND).

503.description: The light could not be read, so it was not snapshotted (SNAPSHOT_UNREADABLE), or this module has no directory to keep one in (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The light's name on these routes: its address without the scheme, so that it is one path segment. http://10.0.0.136 is 10.0.0.136 here, and GET /controllers carries it as name.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The snapshot's id, as GET /devices/{name}/snapshot reports it: the light's name and the moment it was taken, such as 10.0.0.136-20261119T183002Z.

get.summary: One snapshot, with what a restore would send and what it would not
get.description: One snapshot by id, with the sizes of the three documents it holds, everything a restore would write and everything it refuses to, and whether this build can build a body from it at all. The restore table is worked out here and not only at restore time because the page that offers the button is the page that has to show it: light, def, if, timers, um, ap, id and the presets are written; rev, vid, hw, ol, ota, remote and wifi are not, each with its reason; and the network section nw is written whole except for nw.ins, because a configuration write that omits nw clears the light's linked remote. Nothing here touches a light. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The snapshot, and what restoring it would do.

restorable.description: False when this build cannot build a restore body from this file, in which case unrestorable says why.

404.description: This module drives no light of that name, or holds no snapshot of that id for it (CONTROLLER_NOT_FOUND, SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND).

503.description: This module has no snapshot folder to read (STORE_UNAVAILABLE).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The light's name on these routes: its address without the scheme, so that it is one path segment. http://10.0.0.136 is 10.0.0.136 here, and GET /controllers carries it as name.

post.summary: Put a snapshot's configuration back on its light, and wait for it to answer
post.description: Writes a snapshot's configuration back onto the light it was taken from, asks the light to reload it, and waits for it to answer before answering this call: a restore that reported success while the light was mid-reload would be a lie the page believes. It is the one route in this module that rewrites a controller's own configuration, so it refuses more than it accepts. The body must carry confirm: true, and that is checked before the snapshot is even read. The snapshot must have been taken from this light - same address, same controller name - and from a display of the same shape and pixel count, or the restore is refused: a configuration written to another display is a scrambled picture. A safety snapshot of the light as it is now is taken and kept before anything is written, and its id is in every answer that follows, so a restore that went wrong is reversible; a light that cannot be copied is not restored at all. The network section is written whole except for nw.ins. The firmware revision, the hardware revision and the wifi credentials are never written, so this is not a hundred-per-cent clone and the answer says so. The wait is nine seconds, under the ten the host allows a call; the measured restart on the operator's strip is 5.7 seconds and the answer carries that measurement beside this light's own. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

snapshot.description: The id of a snapshot GET /devices/{name}/snapshot reports.

confirm.description: True to mean it. A restore rewrites the light's whole configuration and restarts it, and false is refused before the snapshot is read.

200.description: The configuration was written, the restart was asked for, and the light answered again inside the wait.

complete_clone.description: Always false: no snapshot holds the wifi password, so no restore is a clone of the device.

400.description: The body is not a restore request (RESTORE_BODY_INVALID). Nothing was changed.

404.description: This module drives no light of that name, or holds no snapshot of that id for it (CONTROLLER_NOT_FOUND, SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND).

409.description: The restore was not confirmed (RESTORE_NOT_CONFIRMED), or it was refused: another light's snapshot, another display's shape, a light that did not answer when asked who it is, or a controller that refused the write (RESTORE_REFUSED). Nothing was written, or the detail names the safety snapshot that puts the light back.

503.description: The light could not be read, so the safety snapshot a restore takes first could not be taken, or this module has no directory to keep it in (SNAPSHOT_UNREADABLE, STORE_UNAVAILABLE). Nothing was written.

504.description: The configuration was written and the light has not answered again inside the wait (RESTORE_NOT_ANSWERED). It may still have worked; the safety snapshot named in the detail puts the light back either way.

get.description: What the module holds, and the principal the host authorized, which is the host's answer and never a header the caller set. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

200.description: The module's answer.

principal.description: Who the host says is calling.

State.description: One row of the state table: a state, the colour it is drawn in, the word that replaces the state's own picture while it holds, and where each of the three came from. The ten states that are kind state are the words the host reports; the two that are kind condition are Disconnected and Stale, which this module computes from the reading because the host has no word for either.

state.description: The state's name: IDLE, BUSY, READY, PRINTING, PAUSED, FINISHED, STOPPED, ATTENTION, ERROR or UNKNOWN, or one of the conditions Disconnected and Stale.

kind.description: state for a word the host reports, condition for one of the two this module computes from the reading.

colour.description: The colour the state is drawn in, one byte per channel.

colour_origin.description: store when somebody set this colour and it was kept, default when it is the colour Appendix A gives the state and internal/render draws.

word.description: The text the panel draws for this state while it holds, and empty for no word, which is the default. A word beats the layout composer: a light showing PRINTING shows that word and not the bar and digits. A strip cannot carry one.

word_origin.description: store when somebody wrote this word, default when the state carries none.

holds.description: How long the word holds before the state's own picture comes back. forever is one of the four accepted values and not the absence of one; it is the default.

holds_origin.description: store when somebody chose this hold, default when it is forever because nobody did.

overridden.description: True when any of the three came from the store, which is what decides whether a screen offers a reset.

meaning.description: What the state means, in one line, so that a screen does not have to hold its own copy of Appendix A's prose.

StateRequest.description: One state's row as a caller writes it. At least one of the three is required: a body carrying none of them is refused, because clearing a row is what DELETE is for and a mistyped key must not reset one in silence.

colour.description: The colour to draw the state in: three channels of 0-255, refused with the number in it when a channel is outside that.

word.description: The text the panel draws for this state. Free text, trimmed of surrounding spaces, and an empty word means the state carries none. The limit is the font rather than this route: a character the panel cannot draw is a gap on the light, and the screen warns about it rather than the write refusing it.

holds.description: How long the word holds: forever by default, with 30 s, 60 s and 5 min available. Anything else is refused by name rather than rounded.

Moment.description: One moment a light has, with one entry per printer on that light. The moment belongs to the light and the entry to the (light, printer) pair, which is what lets the same printer show one thing in the office and another in the workshop.

moment.description: The moment's name: print-finished, print-started, filament-change, paused, error-or-attention, light-lost, print-cancelled or printer-went-quiet.

label.description: The words the approved Events screen prints for it, such as Print finished.

meaning.description: What the moment is, in one line.

entries.description: One entry per printer on the light, in the operator's order. One printer is one entry, which is the flat table the screen draws.

printer_count.description: How many printers this moment carries an entry for on this light, which is how the screen knows to indent sub-rows.

MomentEntry.description: What one moment does on one printer on one light: whether it is on, what it shows, which of those it shows, for how long — and where that answer came from.

printer.description: The host's device id for the printer this entry is about.

printer_name.description: The name an operator gave the machine, absent when the host could not be read.

segment.description: The segment that printer is on, on this light, and -1 for the whole light.

whole.description: True when that printer drives the whole light.

enabled.description: Whether the moment is shown at all.

shows.description: What the moment shows: one of the light's own presets, a word on a panel, one of the state table's colours, or nothing.

which.description: Which one of those: a preset's name as WLED spells it, the text to draw for a Word, a state's name for a Colour, and empty for Nothing.

for.description: How long the moment is shown: forever, meaning until the light's own state changes, or a duration such as 60s or 5m.

origin.description: store when somebody edited this entry, default when it is what a delete would put back: for the finished moment on, showing this build's word for a minute; for every other moment, off and showing nothing.

MomentRequest.description: One moment's entry for one printer, as a caller writes it. enabled and shows are required, because a body that forgets them would switch a moment off in silence.

printer.description: The printer this entry is for, by the device id GET /printers carries. Required when the light carries more than one printer and refused with the ones it carries; absent on a light carrying one, where there is nothing to choose.

enabled.description: Whether the moment is shown. Required: an absent value is refused rather than read as off.

shows.description: What the moment shows. Required. A Word is panel only: a strip shows the moment's colour instead.

which.description: A preset's name as WLED spells it, stored as written and never checked against the light, because a write must not fail because a lamp is unplugged; the text to draw for a Word; a state's name for a Colour; and empty for Nothing, where a which is refused rather than dropped.

for.description: How long the moment is shown: forever, meaning until the light's own state changes, or a positive duration such as 60s or 5m. Absent is forever.

Binding.description: One printer, shown on one segment of one controller. One printer may appear in two bindings on two lights, which is what multi-room is; a segment never appears in two.

id.description: The binding's name on these routes: the host's device id for the printer it shows while that printer has one binding, and <device id>@<light>:<segment> once it has two. It is minted once and never changed, so a path a screen holds keeps working.

position.description: Where the binding sits in the operator's order, counting from one.

printer.description: The host's device id for the printer being watched. Two bindings may carry the same one.

printer_name.description: The name an operator gave the machine, absent when the host could not be read.

light.description: The light this binding is on, by the name GET /controllers gives it: the controller's address without the scheme.

controller.description: The controller as the operator wrote it: a base URL with no path.

segment.description: The segment this binding drives, and -1 for the whole controller.

whole.description: True when this binding drives the whole controller, which is the same thing segment -1 says in the shape a person reads.

brightness.description: Written once at start, 0-255, and absent on a borrowed segment where nothing writes one.

BindingRequest.description: One binding as a caller writes it: the same four keys one line of the bindings setting carries.

printer.description: The printer to watch, by the device id GET /printers carries or by the name an operator gave it. On a change it may be left out, and one that names another printer than the binding shows is refused: the binding's own name is in the path.

controller.description: The WLED controller to drive, as its base URL such as http://10.0.0.136, with no path and no trailing slash.

segment.description: The one segment to drive on a controller that carries several, or -1 or absent for the whole controller.

brightness.description: Written once at start, and only on a binding that drives the whole controller: a brightness is controller-wide, so one on a borrowed segment is refused. Absent on a whole-controller binding means 128.

Controller.description: One controller the running set drives, and the bindings that drive it.

name.description: The controller's name on these routes: its address without the scheme, so that it is one path segment.

address.description: The controller as an operator wrote it.

key.description: The same controller with its scheme and host lowercased, which is what the rules compare so that two spellings of one address are one controller.

whole.description: The printer whose binding drives the whole controller, absent when none does.

segments.description: The segments the bindings on this controller borrow, in the operator's order. Never the segments the controller holds: that list is the segments member of GET /controllers/{name}, which asks the controller for it.

printers.description: The device ids of every printer shown on this controller, in the operator's order.

Segment.description: One segment of a light, as the controller reports it. The four bounds keep the controller's own spelling because a caller reads them beside the same four keys in the controller's /json/state and writes them back in a segment write.

id.description: The segment's number: what a binding names and what every write addresses.

name.description: The segment's own name, as it was given in WLED's own interface. Empty on a segment that was never named.

start.description: The first column it covers, inclusive.

stop.description: The column after its last one, exclusive, as WLED defines it.

startY.description: The first row it covers, inclusive, on a 2D controller. Zero on a strip, which has no rows.

stopY.description: The row after its last one, exclusive, on a 2D controller. Zero on a strip, which has no rows, and always carried: a 2D segment whose rows were left out reads as row zero.

id.description: The host's id for the printer, which is what a binding names and what survives a rename.

name.description: The name an operator gave the machine.

connected.description: Whether the host holds a session for it now.

bound_count.description: How many bindings show this printer: 0 for none, 1 for the ordinary case, and 2 or more for a printer in more than one room.

Bound.description: A binding that shows one printer. It is the first of them when a printer sits on more than one light; bound_count says how many there are.

id.description: The binding's name on these routes.

light.description: The light it is shown on, by the name GET /controllers gives it.

controller.description: The controller it is shown on.

segment.description: The segment it drives, and -1 for the whole controller.

whole.description: True when it drives the whole controller.

BindingStatus.description: One binding's answer on the status route: the reading, the frame and the last send, with the controller and segment they belong to.

controller.description: The controller as the operator wrote it.

segment.description: The segment this binding drives, and -1 for the whole controller.

printer.description: The printer being watched, as the single-frame answer describes it.

reading.description: How old the newest fact about the printer is.

frame.description: What the light is being asked to show.

last_send.description: What the last write to the controller did, and null before the first one has been attempted.

Layout.description: One binding's layout: whether the bar is drawn and in which band, how thick it is, whether the percentage and the job's name are drawn and at what scale, and whether the two take turns or sit side by side. Every value carries the origin it came from, which is store when this binding has a row in this module's configuration store and default when it has none; a layout nobody has edited therefore reads as the built-in default rather than as an empty object. remaining is always false and is reported rather than omitted, because the approved mockup draws the control and this build draws no time remaining. rotation_note is present only when the rotation was set to side-by-side, and says what that arrangement draws: the digits on the left at a capped scale, the job's name on the right cut to the room that is left.

id.description: The binding's name on these routes: the host's device id while one printer is shown once, and <device id>@<light>:<segment> once it is shown twice.

printer.description: The host's device id for the printer the binding shows.

light.description: The light the binding sits on.

segment.description: The segment the binding drives, -1 for the whole light.

whole.description: True when the binding drives its whole light.

bar.description: Whether the progress bar is drawn.

bar_band.description: Which end of the panel the bar sits at.

bar_rows.description: How many rows of a 64-row panel the bar takes, 1 to 48.

percent.description: Whether the job's progress is drawn in digits.

percent_scale.description: The scale the digits are drawn at.

name.description: Whether the job's own name is drawn.

rotation.description: How the percentage and the name share the panel. side-by-side puts the digits on the left and the job's name on the right, cut to the room that is left.

rotate_seconds.description: How long each half holds the panel, in seconds.

remaining.description: Always false: this build draws no time remaining.

origin.description: store when this binding has a row in the store, default when it has none.

overridden.description: True when anything about this layout came from the store, which is what decides whether a screen offers a reset.

rotation_note.description: Present only when rotation is side-by-side: what this build does instead.

LayoutRequest.description: One layout as a caller writes it. Every key is optional and every key that is left out goes back to its default, because the write replaces the row rather than merging into it. A body carrying none of them is refused rather than read as "clear the row", because clearing is what DELETE is for.

bar_band.description: Which end of the panel the bar sits at.

bar_rows.description: How many rows the bar takes of a 64-row panel.

percent.description: Draw the job's progress in digits.

percent_scale.description: The scale the digits are drawn at.

remaining.description: May only be false: this build draws no time remaining, so true is refused rather than ignored.

rotation.description: How the percentage and the name share the panel. side-by-side puts the digits on the left and the job's name on the right, cut to the room that is left.

rotate_seconds.description: How long each half holds the panel.

Window.description: One brightness window: a span of the day and the brightness to run at inside it. index is the window's position in the list and the name these routes address it by. wraps_midnight says the end precedes the start, which is the evening window rather than a mistake. active says whether the window contains the instant of the answer, judged in the zone named beside the list, and is absent when this module has no zone to judge it in. wins is true on the one window the list would follow: more than one may be active when they overlap, and the first one wins.

index.description: The window's position in the list, counting from zero.

days.description: The days the window covers. Empty covers every day.

span.description: The two ends as the parser normalised them, such as 20:00-07:00.

wraps_midnight.description: True when the end precedes the start.

active.description: Whether the window contains the instant of the answer, in the zone named beside the list.

wins.description: True on the one window the list would follow at that instant.

WindowRequest.description: One brightness window as a caller writes it, in the same shape the brightness_schedule setting carries, so that a window written here and one written in the settings file mean the same thing.

from.description: When the window opens, as a time of day written HH:MM.

to.description: When it closes, HH:MM. An end earlier than the start wraps midnight and is accepted.

days.description: The days the window covers. Leave it out to cover every day.

WindowsAnswer.description: The brightness windows, judged. judged_in is the IANA zone the windows are read in — the timezone setting — and now is the instant they were judged at, in that zone. Both are always present, because a brightness window an hour wrong is worse than none and these two are how a person checks. wins and level name the window in force at now and the brightness it asks for, and both are absent when none is in force.

judged_in.description: The zone the windows were judged in: the timezone setting's own name, empty when it names nothing.

now.description: The instant the windows were judged at, RFC 3339 in that zone.

wins.description: The index of the window in force at now, absent when none is.

level.description: The brightness the winning window asks for.

Pause.description: One pause. on is computed from the clock at read time and never cached; expired says the row is still in the store with its instant behind it, which is a different answer from nobody having set one. why names the scope the pause is. until is the absolute instant it ends at, in UTC, and forever says in one word that it does not end. effect is what the pause does to its binding: off, or hands-back for a borrowed zone.

printer.description: The binding a binding-scoped pause is about.

on.description: Whether the pause is in force now.

expired.description: True when the row is still stored and its instant has passed.

until.description: The absolute instant this pause ends at, RFC 3339 in UTC. Absent for forever.

forever.description: True when the pause does not end.

remaining_seconds.description: How long is left, when the pause is on.

set_at.description: When the pause was set, RFC 3339 in UTC.

PauseRequest.description: How long a pause lasts. The six are refused by name rather than rounded, because a pause of about an hour is not the thing anybody asked for.

Refusal.description: An RFC 9457 problem naming one of this module's registered codes, as faults.go registers it.

title.description: The English title of the code.

detail.description: What went wrong, in the module's own words.

code.description: The registered code, such as BINDING_REFUSED. Branch on this and not on the sentence.

retryable.description: Whether sending the same request again can work.

SnapshotDevice.description: The light a snapshot was taken from: this module's name for it, the light's own name, its firmware, and the display it was configured for. It is what a restore is checked against before anything is written.

name.description: The light's name on these routes: its address without the scheme.

controller.description: The name the light calls itself, from its /json/info.

Snapshot.description: One snapshot of one light: its configuration, its presets and its state, kept as a file of its own in the directory this module was granted.

id.description: The snapshot's name on these routes, and its file's name: the light and the moment, such as 10.0.0.136-20261119T183002Z.

taken_at.description: When the light was read, RFC 3339 in UTC.

presets.description: How many preset slots it defines, not counting slot 0.

omits.description: What this snapshot cannot give back, worked out from the bytes it holds: always nw.ins, and the wifi password, which no configuration dump on the lights this build was measured against carries.

complete_clone.description: Always false: a literal hundred-per-cent clone is impossible over the API.

RestorePlan.description: What a restore writes and what it refuses to, worked out from one snapshot before anything is sent.

sections.description: The sections written, in the order they go out: light, def, if, timers, um, ap, id, and presets when the snapshot holds a table.

withheld.description: The sections of the dump that are not written, each with its reason: rev and vid by the requirements, hw, ol, ota, remote and wifi because the requirements' restore table does not list them.

nw.description: The network section is sent whole except for its credential, because a configuration write that omits it clears the light's linked remote.

members_removed.description: The members of the network section that are not written back. ins, the credential.

presets.description: True when the snapshot's preset table is written with the configuration.

Reboot.description: What a restore measured while it waited for the light to answer again.

requested.description: Always true: the restart is asked for in the body that was written.

observed.description: True when at least one poll failed, so the light was seen to go away and come back. False means it answered throughout, which is reported rather than glossed.

first_refusal_seconds.description: From the write to the first poll that failed. Absent when no poll failed.

answered_after_seconds.description: From the write to the first answer this module believed, which is the first one at least a second after the write.

outage_seconds.description: From the first refusal to the answer: how long the light was away. Absent when it never went away.

measured_reference.description: The hand measurement this route was built from: the first refusal and the first answer, on the operator's own strip.

FrameAnswer.description: One binding's frame for the Overview screen: what this module decided, how old the reading is, and the picture itself.

binding.description: The printer this binding shows, by the device id the binding routes use.

segment.description: The segment this binding drives, and -1 for the whole light.

width.description: The picture's width in pixels: the light's own, or the borrowed run's.

frame.description: The frame this module decided: colour, lit, total, percent, name and reason.

reading.description: How old the reading behind the picture is, and whether it is stale.

last_send.description: What the last write to the light did.

base64.description: The PNG, base64-encoded: the data URL is data: followed by media_type, a semicolon, base64, a comma, then this string.

cached.description: True when this answer was served from the cache against the same frame.

note.description: What a person has to know to read the picture honestly: a stale reading's age, or why a frame could not be drawn.
